subject: Intermittent internal API failures after private cutover — possible SNAT/MTU interaction
messages:

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T23:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Private cutover — intermittent internal API failures

Sara — thanks for the heads up. We're opening an incident on our side and looping in infra/networking. Can you confirm whether the failures are observed for traffic that originates and terminates inside your VPC (service-to-service), or only when hitting the private load balancer/edge? Also please attach one representative pcap and a short curl trace from a failed request.

Action items I need from you to triage quickly:
- One pcap (packet capture) showing a failed transaction (TCP reset/ICMP fragmentation)
- A tcpdump around the time of failure (10s before/after)
- The curl -v output and the exact endpoints used (hostnames/IPs)

We're cc'ing Karthik and Marissa for route/NAT/MTU checks. I'll coordinate a play-by-play and temporary mitigations.

Thanks,

From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: NimbusCloud Network Ops <netops@nimbuscloud.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T00:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Private cutover — intermittent internal API failures

Hi Tessa — attaching the pcaps and a short curl trace. Symptoms: internal service A -> service B calls intermittently see TLS handshake timeouts and connection resets. Both services are in the same VPC subnet post-cutover, but path traverses our NAT gateway and the edge LB (we used the redwood-private-handoff). Failures started ~2027-03-29T22:40Z after we shifted traffic.

Observations from our telemetry:
- Some TCP flows show MSS/MTU mismatch and ICMP "Fragmentation needed" messages, but not for every flow.
- When flows get reset, the SYN reaches the target but the response sometimes never completes the handshake.
- We also see source IP translation inconsistencies: sometimes client IP is preserved, sometimes SNATed to the same ephemeral range — hard to correlate.

Attachments: nimbus_pcap_20270329.pcap (10s window), edge_routes_snapshot.json, curl_trace.txt

Thanks,
Sara Lin
Engineering Manager — NimbusCloud Platform

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T02:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Private cutover — intermittent internal API failures

Quick summary of what I see after an initial pass on the artifacts Sara provided:
- PCAP shows a pattern where MSS negotiation from the client is 1460, but along the path an intermediate device (our edge LB) sets DF and MTU is effectively lower on the next hop. A few flows receive ICMP "fragmentation needed" and then the handshake stalls. This matches classic PMTU blackhole behavior in mixed MTU segments.
- More interesting: flows that traverse the SNAT path show inconsistent source translation. I can see both original pod IPs and SNATed addresses in responses, which suggests two different egress datapaths are in play (one bypasses SNAT, one uses SNAT pool). That would explain why some flows succeed and others fail even between the same endpoints.

Hypothesis: During the cutover we introduced parallel forwarding entries — one path goes through the private edge appliance (MTU-limited), the other is direct via the customer's NAT gateway (preserves MTU but may SNAT differently). Asymmetric routing + one path hitting PMTU issue + inconsistent SNAT is causing intermittent failures.

Short-term mitigation suggestions:
- Temporarily force service-to-service flows to prefer the path that preserves MSS (if Nimbus can route via the direct path) to confirm hypothesis.
- On Redwood side, we can add an MTU clamp on the edge to avoid DF+fragmentation (set MSS clamp to 1380) and ensure consistent SNAT mapping by pinning the SNAT pool for the affected subnet. I can push a config but need approval.

I'll prepare a minimal runbook and a difflist for the config change.

Karthik
Principal Network Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
[internal note: see trace id NET-712]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T09:17:00Z
Subject: Re: Private cutover — intermittent internal API failures

Sara — thanks for the quick data and team, appreciate the patience. We've validated Karthik's hypothesis with the attached traces. Plan of action (agreed rollback-safe steps):

1) Immediate mitigation (10–30 min, no downtime):
   - Redwood will apply an MTU/MSS clamp of 1380 on the private edge appliance (non-disruptive to established TCP sessions). This avoids PMTU blackhole effects for new handshakes.
   - We will also pin the SNAT pool for the affected internal ASN so that source translation is consistent across egress paths.

2) Short follow-up (1–6 hours):
   - Nimbus to temporarily route inter-service traffic via the direct path (bypass-edge) for confirmation. If stability improves, we know edge MTU as root cause.
   - We'll coordinate a maintenance window if we need to change route policies.

3) Postmortem and durable fix (24–72 hours):
   - Root-cause: remove the parallel forwarding entries that cause asymmetric egress.
   - Add monitoring to detect SNAT churn and PMTU ICMP rates.

Attachments: redwood_trace_20270329.txt (edge trace), runbook link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=runbook-priv-cutover, Jira: https://redwood-internal.atlassian.net/browse/NET-712

If you approve, we'll proceed with the immediate mitigation now and keep you updated every 15 minutes until stable.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
